address: SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53, PCI DSS, HIPAA

reading.body:
CoreSite AT2 publishes 67,000 square feet of technical space and no IT load figure in megawatts. Without a published power number, translating that footprint into racks or accelerators requires an assumption about power density, and CoreSite has not supplied one, so this site will not fabricate that figure. What the square footage does establish is a mid-sized colocation floor, meaningful for enterprise workloads but not in the range of the hundred-megawatt hyperscale campuses now dominating AI infrastructure conversation.

The certifications, taken one at a time, qualify the campus to host regulated financial data under SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2, payment card environments under PCI DSS, protected health information under HIPAA, information security management systems under ISO 27001, and federal-aligned security controls under NIST 800-53. Collectively they position AT2 for compliance-sensitive enterprise tenants. None of the certifications speak to AI training density, power redundancy tier, or cooling architecture, and those specs are not published.

Georgia has 33 mapped facilities in this site's index, but only 2 of those publish a megawatt figure, totaling 42 MW combined. AT2 ranks third in the state by published megawatts, which means it falls below both facilities that do publish power, but its own power figure is not published, so the ranking reflects an absence of data rather than a confirmed smaller footprint. For a reader sizing up Georgia as an AI compute region, the state's 42 MW of confirmed published capacity is a thin picture, and AT2's missing power figure leaves its contribution to that picture unknown.
